profile.headline: Staff Software Engineer at SoFi
profile.geoLocationName: Salt Lake City, Utah, United States

positions.title: Senior Android Engineer
positions.description: Sorenson's video relay service empowers the deaf and hard-of-hearing community to communicate with both deaf and hearing people. As an Android developer, I work on the ntouch® Mobile app available on the Google Play Store. I write code daily in Kotlin and Java and perform code reviews using Github. I follow the Material Design guidelines, work with our UX designer and listen closely to our users in order to provide the best mobile VRS experience.

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description: Using my existing expertise with mobile data terminals and my passion for Android development, I was part of the development team building the Android ROM for Micronet's A-317® and SmartHub® mobile data terminals. Using the Java Native Interface I wrote Java APIs for partners building Android apps on our mobile data terminals. These Android tablets were designed and built to be used in harsh environmental conditions, so I worked closely with our electrical and mechanical engineers to build reliability software programs in Java and C++ for stress tests and troubleshooting.

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description: I developed applications in C++ and C# for use on our TREQ mobile data terminals. Being motivated to learn new software systems and languages provided me with opportunities to make valuable upgrades to existing software systems. I used SVN and Git on a daily basis for our final test software (C++) and ERP system (PHP/MySQL).

positions.title: Applications Engineer
positions.description: I provided application development support for software developers building on our TREQ platform. The TREQ®-M4 and TREQ®-VM mobile data terminals are premium rugged terminals built and designed to withstand harsh environmental conditions. As an Applications Engineer I was required to quickly solve problems that were complex and unique to the field. I worked closely with Beijer's firmware engineers to write sample applications in C++ and C# for our hardware devices. Since I was working closely with the firmware and device drivers, I became familiar with making managed .NET calls to native code using PInvoke.
